payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones

decision.question: Does comparison of the source and edited images establish that the source mug has been relocated to the right of the headphones?
decision.criteria: Pass when visual correspondence and spatial evidence support that the source mug has been relocated to the right of the headphones in the edited image. Evaluate correspondence using the combined evidence of body proportions, rim, handle geometry, scale, appearance, and placement; exact color or appearance preservation is not required. A mug on the right alone does not establish the requested relocation. Fail when the evidence establishes that the source mug remains left of the headphones or otherwise has not reached the requested right-side position, including identifiable movement that stops short of that position. Use unknown when competing correspondences remain unresolved and would change whether the condition is satisfied. Neither failure to prove completion nor a blurred remnant alone establishes failure.
decision.binding: Target: the light-blue mug with a left-facing handle in the source image. Reference: the headphones in each image. Compare that mug with both edited mugs—the pale mug left of the headphones and the mug right of them—and inspect the blue blurred patch at far left as possible residual evidence. Assess the candidates without assigning identity from color alone or requiring an unchanged handle orientation. Account for the different image framing, scale, and headphone arrangement by comparing object-relative positions rather than raw pixel coordinates. Determine whether the combined evidence establishes relocation of the source mug to the right of the edited headphones; leave the result unknown if the available evidence cannot resolve that condition.
